reason: Domain glossary. Terms here are the vocabulary of the PRD and the code — Topic, Project, Project Mention, Published Project, Single Worker, Cursor, Four States. Use these words, do not invent synonyms.

Root architecture map: the single-Worker topology, the routing split between the asset router and Python, and the platform limits table (cron CPU 10ms Free / 30s Paid, 50 vs 10000 subrequests, 6 concurrent connections). These numbers constrain the design, not just the deployment.

The ten Python Workers runtime rules that fail only after deploy: entrypoint must be class Default(WorkerEntrypoint), asgi.entrypoint provides no scheduled(), env is attribute-access-only, no self.env in ASGI routes, src/ is not on the import path, compatibility_date is frozen, requirements.txt aborts pywrangler, triggers.crons replaces on deploy, no threading, keep global scope cheap. Read before writing any backend code.

The Minimal v7.7.0 whitelist port: what was copied, what was dropped, and the five surgeries applied to the vendored theme. Explains why @mui/x-date-pickers is a type-only devDependency and why icon-sets.ts is trimmed to 13 icons. Read before touching theme/, layouts/ or components/.

The import boundaries: domain/ may import stdlib only; a JsProxy may not leave persistence/d1.py; SQL lives in module constants so tests can import it. Violating these breaks the fast pure test suite.

D1 without transactions: claim-by-conditional-UPDATE with meta.changes, idempotency by unique constraint plus ON CONFLICT, the 100-bound-parameter ceiling, keyset pagination, and the single ISO 8601 UTC millisecond timestamp format the schema's TEXT comparisons depend on.
Retryable vs permanent vs configuration failures, why run_sync never raises, and why per-topic isolation is per-task try/except rather than gather(return_exceptions=True).
What may be logged (ids, exception class names, bounded categories) and what must never be (LLM payloads, secrets, full response bodies). The PRD makes this a security requirement.
The only coupling surface between frontend and backend. snake_case on the wire, next_cursor === null as the sole end-of-list signal, and the list of fields the API must never expose.
TanStack Query conventions, the cursor-pagination hook shape, and the four required states in priority order. The isPending-vs-isFetching distinction is the one most likely to be got wrong.
sx-only styling (MUI v9 removed system props), RouterLink takes href not to, external links need rel=noopener noreferrer, and typed icon names.
Where a file goes, and the machine-enforced import group order — features/* sorts before components/*, which is the most common lint failure.
Why one Worker and not two, why @cloudflare/vite-plugin cannot be used with a .py entrypoint, why run_worker_first is an array, and why the MVP has no CORS.
Why TanStack Query rather than the template's SWR, with the evidence. Prevents re-litigating the data layer.
Four frontend dependencies are pinned behind latest for verified peer-constraint reasons (typescript-eslint requires TS <6.1, eslint-plugin-import caps at ESLint 9). Read before upgrading anything.

Verified shape of the real RSSHub feed: RSS 2.0, item has only title/description/link/guid/pubDate, the linux.do topic URL is inside the description HTML with a floor suffix, and link points at Telegram. The channel reader must not rely on the link field.

The Responses API contract: strict text.format JSON Schema, no silent fallback to Chat Completions, Pydantic revalidation at the boundary, and the candidate-allowlist rule that prevents repository hallucination.
